title: EKS blueprint provisioner: preflight validations, canary cluster and safe control-plane upgrades
creator: Aisha Morgan
description: Build a reusable Terraform module (eks-blueprint-provisioner) for Redwood Private control plane provisioning that adds deterministic preflight checks, a canary cluster workflow for safe EKS control-plane and node upgrades, and opinionated health checks. The module will be used by the Private control-plane installer (VPC deployments) and must support: cross-account KMS keys, S3 remote state with locking, provider aliasing for multi-region builds, configurable endpoint access (private/public), and integration hooks for our rollout automation. Goal: reduce upgrade incidents and shorten mean-time-to-repair for control-plane issues during customer on-prem/VPC upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes a stable inputs/outputs contract and passes terraform validate/fmt/lint in CI
Module runs end-to-end in a staged environment and produces an EKS control plane + managed nodegroups with tags and IAM roles applied
Preflight command (terraform apply -target=module.preflight) runs and flags quota/networking/iam issues with clear remediation steps
A canary cluster can be provisioned using module.canary with automated smoke checks and automatic rollback on failure
Health-check SNS/CloudWatch alerts and Prometheus scrape configs created by module match the on-call runbook expectations
State migration documented: existing control-plane stacks can be imported into the new module without cluster downtime
technical_design: High-level design: 1) Module split: core (eks_controlplane), network (vpc_subnets_route), iam (roles_policies), observability (cloudwatch_prometheus_bridge), preflight (validations), and canary (cluster_canary). 2) State: S3 backend with DynamoDB lock table; workspaces for env isolation. 3) Providers: aws providers aliased for management and target accounts; explicit region and partition handling. 4) KMS: customer-managed KMS alias creation in target account with separate key policy for cross-account access. 5) Upgrades: control-plane upgrades executed via canary cluster first; if canary passes smoke tests, rollout plan updates module variable control_plane_version to trigger blue-green-like upgrade using node rotation and API server version bump. 6) Health: deploy a lightweight helm chart (redwood-controlplane-exporter) backed by PrometheusRules and CloudWatch dashboards; include synthetic probes (SLO) for API responsiveness, etcd leader change rate, and certificate expiry monitoring.
module_interface_notes: Inputs: env_name, account_id, region, vpc_id (optional), public_subnets, private_subnets, cluster_endpoint_access (private|public|both), kms_key_alias, control_plane_version, node_groups (list), canary_enabled (bool as string 'true'|'false'), preflight_skip_checks (list). Outputs: cluster_name, cluster_endpoint, kubeconfig_s3_path, kms_key_arn, nodegroup_arns.
migration_steps: 1) Run preflight against existing stack to collect resource IDs. 2) Create a migration workspace and S3/Dynamo backend for module-managed state. 3) Use terraform import to bring in EKS cluster resource and critical IAM roles into the module-managed state. 4) Validate imported state by running 'terraform plan' in dry-run. 5) Flip kubeconfig_s3_path to new module location during a low-traffic window. 6) Run canary upgrade flow against a fresh canary cluster before any control-plane version changes on prod.
test_plan: Unit: terraform validate + tflint + checkov in GH actions. Integration: terratest suite (Go) that spins up a minimal cluster in a sandbox account, runs preflight, verifies nodegroup lifecycle hooks, and tears down. Smoke: automated smoke tests that exercise API server, list nodes, run sample inference workload pod, and run synthetic latency SLO probe. Chaos: run a simulated AZ failure in sandbox and assert health checks and auto-recovery hooks.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): merge module into infra repo; enable canary_enabled for staging and run full terratest. Phase 2 (pilot): provision canary cluster in pilot customer account with monitoring and on-call watch. Phase 3 (gradual rollout): schedule weekly upgrade windows; run canary ref for each control_plane_version; proceed to prod only after 48h of stable metrics. Rollback: module supports revert by setting control_plane_version back to previous and nodegroup version pinning; we will automate snapshotting of etcd via AWS Backup before each upgrade.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: terraform import mismatches cause drift — Mitigation: build import helpers script and preflight checks that validate resource IDs and tags before importing
Risk: KMS cross-account policy errors — Mitigation: template policy tests and cross-account access tests in terratest; require security review before production rollout
Risk: Canaries not representative of production — Mitigation: make canary footprint configurable to mimic customer-sized nodegroups; include perf profile checks
Risk: State locking misconfigurations across regions — Mitigation: enforce single DynamoDB lock table per environment and validate backend during CI
